speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me if you have experienced any headaches, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light along with your fever? Also, have you had any recent travel or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your use of haloperidol, I need to check for signs of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome; do you have any significant muscle rigidity or sweating? Let me perform a quick physical exam to assess your muscle tone and check for any fever-induced sweating.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, generalized rigidity, altered mentation, and autonomic instability (profuse sweating) in the context of haloperidol use is highly suggestive of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I need to rule out other causes and assess for rhabdomyolysis, so REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase, Complete Blood Count, and Electrolytes.
